LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.7: MONEY
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers MONEY, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can you save money?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on MONEY together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: as learners in groups discuss and convert shillings into cents and cents into

shillings using real/ imitation money

• Self-efficacy as learners: calculates the total cost of items in the shopping list.

• Creativity and critical thinking: as learners come up with a class or school model shop and role play shopping

activities as buyers and shopkeepers.

Values

• Integrity: Learners in groups/individually correctly calculate the total cost of items in the shopping list.

• Patriotism: As learners display citizenship when converting shillings into cents and cents into shillings which is

Kenyan currency.
